channel.title: Avantis Hub Updates
channel.description: Most recent updates for Avantis Hub

item.title: Version 0.9.12
item.description:
New

  • Macs on different versions can share a setup folder. When the hub saves the boards, the settings or a profile, it now keeps anything a newer version added that it does not understand, such as a new kind of MIDI feedback or a new quick button option, instead of dropping it. Each save also records which version wrote it. If the setup was saved in a newer format than this hub knows, it still opens and runs from it, but saves nothing to it, and a banner at the top of the window asks you to update. The same happens if the boards file cannot be read at all, so the hub never puts a new board over boards it could not see.
  • This protects only from this version on: update every Mac that shares the folder to 0.9.12. Until then, an older hub can still drop what it does not know when it saves.

item.title: Version 0.9.11
item.description:
New

  • Second press undoes it. A quick button option for buttons such as a talk back. While the button is in effect (its mutes and assigns are as it sets them), pressing it again sets them back, puts back the levels it remembered and puts each UFX value it changed back to what it was before. Levels it set to a fixed value stay where they are. Turn it on in the button's editor.
  • MIDI feedback can follow an input's main assign. In Window, MIDI Feedback, choose "An input's main assign": on while the input is on the main mix. A SoftStep key can show whether a singer is singing (green) or in talk back (red).
  • When it connects, the hub now reads each input's main assign (LR) from the console, along with the mutes and send levels, so it knows them without anyone pressing anything.
  • If macOS runs a protected copy of the hub, which happens when it is opened before Finder has moved it to Applications, the hub cannot update itself. It now says so in a banner and in Settings, Updates, with how to fix it.

Fixed

  • A board with MIDI feedback from a later version could not be opened. Feedback the hub does not know is now left out instead.

item.title: Version 0.9.10
item.description:
New

  • MIDI feedback. The hub can send MIDI to a controller or app when something changes, so a pedal's LED can show a singer's tuner, a quick button that is in effect, or a Live track such as Repeat. Set it up in its own window, from Inputs, MIDI or Window, MIDI Feedback: name each device, choose its port on this Mac, and add feedback. A SoftStep key lights green for on and red for off; any other controller or app can be given its own MIDI messages. Nothing is sent to the console.

Fixed

  • In Settings, Console, New Board and Delete Board were cut short beside Copy Settings From, which now has its own line.
  • The Ableton Live address and port labels were in the same monospaced type as their values.
  • The Delete Board dialog said nothing could be undone; its profiles can be brought back with Restore Deleted Profile.
  • The Inputs pill's and the glide picker's tips, and the UFX parameter tip, which now gives the console's path: FX, Rack UltraFX, Show Routing, MIDI Setup.

item.title: Version 0.9.9
item.description:
New

  • Settings that go with the board. A board's Startup settings, OSC port and Ableton Live link (on or off, address, ports, and Press quick buttons from clip names) are now kept with the board instead of on each Mac. With a shared folder, every Mac that opens the board is set up the same way: prepare one Mac, and the other is ready when it opens that board. On the first launch, every board takes this Mac's current settings, so nothing changes until you change it.
  • Copy Settings From. Beside New Board: gives the board in use another board's settings and options, for example after trying them on a replica. It never copies the address, MIDI channel or firmware.
  • If another Mac changes the settings of the board in use while this hub is armed, the change waits behind the same Reload banner as a changed profile. When disarmed, it is taken at once.

Changed

  • AvantisHubOSC. The hub now reads Ableton Live through AvantisHubOSC, a free copy of AbletonOSC made for it (link in the Ableton Live settings and the manual). It has its own ports, 11006 and 11007, so it runs beside AbletonOSC and apps that use it, such as StageView, and it logs far less. New boards use those ports; existing boards keep theirs. Plain AbletonOSC still works on 11000 and 11001.
  • Shorter text across the app: the explanations are in this manual and the FAQ (Help menu). The Ableton Live address and ports are always shown, and are kept when the settings close, without pressing Return.
  • Which other MIDI inputs the hub listens to stays with each Mac, because the same device can have a different name on each Mac, for example through Bome Network.

item.title: Version 0.9.8
item.description:
New

  • Remember and Put back. A quick button's action on a fader or send level can be "Remember, then set to": it keeps the level as it is, then sets the new one. Another button's "Put back" sets it back to what was kept. A second press keeps the first level, and a kept level survives quitting the hub. If the hub does not know a level yet, the button shows a warning triangle and leaves that level alone. Tried on an Avantis with firmware 2.0.1.
  • Sends to the UFX units. An input's send to a UFX send can now be set by a button or mapping, like aux and FX sends. With "Read input mutes and faders on connecting" on, the hub also reads every input's UFX send levels as it connects, so a Remember on one of them works without the send being moved first.
  • The console's tap tempo from Live. A board option, off unless you turn it on: while armed and while Live is playing, Live's tempo sets the console's Global Tap Tempo, which the UFX delays follow. A new tempo goes out once it has held for one beat, so short steps at the ends of songs are left out. The console holds the beat in whole milliseconds, so 114 BPM goes out as 526 ms, and the Monitor shows "Tap tempo → 114 BPM (526 ms)". It is sent on the port Avantis Director uses.
  • "Press quick buttons from clip names". Pressing a quick button from a clip's name on a Hub track in Live is now its own setting, under Ableton Live, and off unless you turn it on. Leave it off if those clips also send the buttons' MIDI notes, or each button is pressed twice.
  • The Help menu tells these pages which version you have, so they can say when they describe a newer one.

Changed

  • Consoles found by Find are listed under their own heading, each with a Use button.
  • The Ableton Live settings name the ports to use with StageView's relay (11004 and 11005), with which StageView and the hub can both read from Live on one Mac.

Fixed

  • If the hub's MIDI port cannot be opened as the hub starts, it tries again every 2 seconds instead of staying failed until the hub is restarted.
  • In the button editor, a level action showed its -inf switch above the row, unlabelled, and cut its target short. -inf is now a choice beside the level, and the target shows in full.
  • "Read input mutes and faders on connecting" failed while Avantis Director was connected to the console at the same time: the console marks its messages differently for a second program, and the hub now reads them.

item.title: Version 0.9.7
item.description:
New

  • More read on connecting. The experimental option is now "Read input mutes and faders on connecting". As well as the inputs' mutes, it reads their fader levels, the DCAs' mutes and levels, the mute groups' mutes, and the mutes and levels of the stereo auxes, the mains and the stereo matrices. It only fills in what the hub does not already know. Still off unless you turn it on.
  • Name your mute groups. The console does not tell the hub their names, so you can give them one: double-click a mute group's name in Show view, or click the pencil beside it in Board Targets.
  • Which tuner button is in effect. A quick button that only sets UFX parameters, such as Tuner On or Tuner Off, shows NOW in Show view while it is the one in effect, going by what the hub last sent.
  • A quieter Monitor. "Only what the hub uses" hides incoming MIDI that nothing is set to, and a run of values from one control folds into one line with a count.
  • Quick buttons have twelve colours to choose from instead of six.
  • A banner for updates. When the daily check finds a new version, a banner across the top of the window says so, with Show Update and Later. Before, the update window could open as the hub started and vanish before it could be read.

Changed

  • UFX keys, scales and parameters go to the console at least 50 ms apart, in the order asked for. The console was seen to miss a key sent right behind another UFX change. Mutes and faders are not held back.
  • A main that is one stereo pair, such as LR, shows once instead of as Main 1 and Main 2.

Fixed

  • A note whose Note Off never arrived, for example because its clip was stopped, no longer blocks the next press of that note. Once nothing has been heard from it for 2 seconds, a new Note On counts again.
  • A keyboard shortcut using an arrow key showed as a question mark, though it worked. Arrows, Return, Tab, Space, Home, End, Page Up, Page Down and F1 to F12 now show by name.

item.title: Version 0.9.6
item.description:
New

  • One switch for UFX cues. Each board has "Send UFX key, scale and parameters" in its Options. With it off, every UFX cue on that board is held and the Monitor says so, while everything else carries on. It starts off: turn it on for a board whose UFX cues you were already using.
  • With Raw bytes ticked, the Monitor shows the exact bytes of each change the hub sends, on a line marked SENT.
  • Switch All On and Switch All Off. The "..." menu at the top of the mapping list switches every mapping in the profile on or off in one step. Undo puts them back.

Changed

  • The mapping list is in order of MIDI channel and then note, with notes before CCs before program changes. OSC addresses and locators follow. Only the list is sorted: mappings on one trigger still fire in the order they were made.
  • A note being released while the hub is disarmed no longer gets a "blocked" line of its own.
  • A profile whose file changes while the hub is running is said to have changed "outside this hub", which is true on one Mac as well as two.

Fixed

  • A profile is saved the same way every time. Before, the same profile could be written out in a different order, which made a shared folder copy it to every Mac for nothing.

item.title: Version 0.9.5
item.description:
New

  • Other MIDI inputs. The hub can listen to a hardware controller, a network MIDI session or any other MIDI input on the Mac, as well as its own port. Switch each one on in the Inputs settings. A dot beside each input lights when it carries MIDI, so you can see which one a controller is on.
  • Find. A button beside Console IP lists the Avantis consoles on the network. Click one to use its address.
  • A console that has moved. When a board will not connect and one console that could be yours answers at another address, a banner offers it. The hub never changes the address by itself.
  • UFX key and scale. On firmware V2.0 and later, a mapping or quick button can set the key and scale the console's UFX pitch effects follow.
  • UFX parameters. A mapping or quick button can set a parameter of a UFX unit, such as a vocal tuner's bypass, once it has a MIDI channel and controller number on the console. Each has a name, kept with the board.
  • SoftKeys and MIDI strips as triggers. A board can take MIDI the console sends from a SoftKey or MIDI strip as a trigger. It is off unless you turn it on.
  • From. A mapping, or a quick button's MIDI trigger, can be tied to one MIDI input, so the same note from another input does nothing.
  • Clicking a target with no mapping selected starts a new mapping for it.

Changed

  • The Inputs settings have a tab each for MIDI, OSC and Ableton Live.
  • The board settings have three tabs, Connection, Options and Startup, with Connect at the bottom of each.
  • The mapping inspector is laid out in rows that line up.
  • The settings windows are as tall as what they hold.

item.title: Version 0.9.4
item.description:
New

  • Firmware V2.0. The hub now reaches inputs 65 to 96, the extra groups, auxes and matrices, and the UFX sends and returns. Each board has a Firmware setting: choose "Before V2.0" for a console on older firmware.
  • Pages in Show view. Build your own tabs of channels in any order, like a custom layer on the console. Click Pages… at the top of the surface.
  • Named. A button in Board Targets and in Show view that hides every channel nobody has named on the console.
  • The search field in Board Targets has a clear button.
  • A Copy button in the Monitor puts every line on the clipboard.
  • Settings > Inputs links to where AbletonOSC can be downloaded.
  • Experimental: a board can read which inputs are muted as it connects, so those mutes are known from the start. It is off unless you turn it on, it only reads, and it should be tried at a quiet console first. See the manual.

Changed

  • A mute the console has not reported yet now reads "MUTE ?" with a dashed edge, so it cannot be taken for a mute that is known to be off.
  • The hub no longer sends a fader the same level twice in a row.
  • The User Manual and FAQ have a contents list down the side, sharper screenshots that open large when clicked, and new sections on firmware, pages and mutes.

Fixed

  • Channel names from the console no longer carry invisible padding, which could stop a name being matched.
  • The hub no longer warns that the two halves of the LR main share a name.

The companion app should be updated alongside this version, so that it knows the new kinds of channel.

item.title: Version 0.9.3
item.description:
Fixed

  • The Use button beside a trigger with a long name is no longer squeezed. The name is shortened instead.
  • The help under Base MIDI channel in Settings is no longer cut off.

item.title: Version 0.9.2
item.description:
Changed

  • The hub now checks for updates even while armed. A hub that is always armed used to miss them altogether.
  • An update found while armed opens no window. An Update marker shows at the top of the window, in the menu bar panel and in Settings, and waits for a click.
  • Installing still asks before it quits an armed hub.

item.title: Version 0.9.1
item.description:
What's New

  • Help menu: the User Manual, FAQ and Release Notes.

This version is mainly here to prove that updating works.
